title: Miketz: at the end of two years (Genesis 41:1, 14)
hookLine: the waiting ends in a day; Joseph is shaved and brought out

cards: Waiting for the call back after the interview. Waiting for the test results, the visa, the transplant list, the baby. Days that feel exactly like the day before.
When Joseph read the cupbearer's dream, he asked him one thing: when you're free, remember me, and mention me to Pharaoh. The cupbearer was freed three days later.
And the Torah says, with brutal simplicity, that he did not remember Joseph. He forgot him. The days go on in the dungeon.

teach.h: AT THE END OF TWO FULL YEARS.
teach.b: The new portion is called Miketz, at the end.

It opens, in the old Jewish Publication Society translation: "And it came to pass at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed." Two full years. Morning after morning in prison, after hope had come so close.
The rabbis asked why two years. An old midrash, which Rashi brings, gives a hard answer: Joseph put his trust in the cupbearer, asking him twice to remember him, and so he waited two more years.
Other teachers push back, gently: asking for help isn't wrong. The Torah itself doesn't say why. It only counts the time.

Then everything changes in a single day. Pharaoh dreams of seven fat cows eaten by seven thin ones, and nobody in Egypt can explain it. The cupbearer suddenly remembers: I have to confess something today.
There was a young Hebrew in prison.

teach.h: BROUGHT HASTILY OUT OF THE DUNGEON.
teach.b: Pharaoh sends for Joseph, and look how fast the verbs move: "they brought him hastily out of the dungeon." He shaves. He changes his clothes.
He walks in before Pharaoh. From the dungeon to the king, with nothing in between but a razor and clean clothes.

teach.h: HELP IN THE BLINK OF AN EYE.
teach.b: There's a Jewish saying: God's help comes in the blink of an eye.
It isn't a promise about when; nobody told Joseph the date. But long waiting and sudden change live side by side. The forgotten prisoner is the one they're running to fetch.
Here, the end came all at once.

how: Miketz is read in synagogues in early winter, and Jews repeat the saying that God's help comes in the blink of an eye, yeshuat Hashem k'heref ayin, in hard times.

games.q: you've been forgotten in prison for two years. suddenly guards run in: Pharaoh wants you now. you're Joseph. what do you do?
o: go as you are, right away.
shave, change your clothes, and go in.
ask why it took so long.
games.why: Joseph shaved, changed his clothes and came in to Pharaoh. the waiting ended in a single day.

practice: Think of something you've been waiting on for a long time, and feel the weight of the waiting, honestly. Then picture Joseph the morning they came running: he shaved, he changed his clothes, he was ready.
What one small thing could you keep in order, so that if the door opens, you can walk through?
